details.title: Crop Basics & Plant Biology
details.content: **Rice (चावल (धान))** is a cereal crop belonging to the family **Poaceae (Gramineae)** (scientific name *Oryza sativa*). It completes its crop cycle in about **110–145 days**. Growth stages follow the sequence germination → seedling → vegetative growth → reproductive phase (flowering/fruiting) → maturity. Main growing states: **Punjab, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Bihar, Assam**. Popular varieties/ hybrids: **BPT 5204, Swarna, IR-64, PR 126, Pusa Basmati 1121, PB-1509**.

details.title: Climate Requirements
details.content: **Rice** thrives in a warm and humid, ideally 25–32 °C with bright sunshine climate with full sun (high light intensity) conditions. Ideal temperature range is **22–32 °C**, relative humidity **60–80%**, and annual rainfall **1000–1800 mm**. Extreme conditions (frost, heat waves, hail or waterlogging) at sensitive stages lower yield and quality.

details.title: Soil Requirements
details.content: The crop grows best in **heavy clay loam to alluvial loam that holds standing water**. Suitable soil pH ranges from **5.5–7**, electrical conductivity (EC) below **<1.5 dS/m**, and organic matter of about **1.0–1.5%**. Adequate soil depth, good drainage, and balanced nutrient status of the soil are prerequisites for a healthy stand.

details.title: Land Preparation
details.content: Land preparation includes **two or three deep ploughings followed by puddling. level the field, maintain 5–10 cm standing water and break the pan for better root anchorage.**. A well-tilled but properly levelled seedbed ensures uniform germination and stand establishment; drainage channels protect against waterlogging in heavy soil and during monsoons.

details.title: Seed & Planting Material
details.content: Use certified material: **Certified seed with 80%+ germination; treat with carbendazim 2 g/kg or Pseudomonas bio-formulation for bakanae & sheath blight prevention.**. Seed/variant rate for main season is **35–45 kg/ha (HYY direct-seeded 60–80 kg/ha)**. Treat seed against soil-borne diseases and, where applicable, inoculate with beneficial rhizobia/PSB before sowing for legumes.

details.title: Sowing & Planting
details.content: **Sowing/planting season:** Kharif: Jun–Jul; Rabi/summer: Dec–Jan. Optimum sowing depth **2–3 cm**, spacing **20 × 15 cm (hills of 3–4 seedlings)**, maintaining a plant population of **≈ 3,00,000 hills/ha (33 hills/m²)**. Correct spacing balances canopy (sunlight) and aeration. Depth and timing should follow regional package-of-practice recommendations.

details.title: Water & Irrigation Management
details.content: Irrigation method: **Flooding / shallow submergence with continuous standing water**. Critical stages — Critical stages: tillering, panicle initiation, flowering; drain 10–14 days before harvest. Typical frequency/quantity: **No fixed count; maintain 3–5 cm water depth till maturity**. Do not let the crop suffer at the most sensitive growth phases (critical stages: tillering, panicle initiation, flowering; drain 10–14 days before harvest); avoid both drought and waterlogging.

details.title: Nutrient Management
details.content: Nutrient schedule: **120:60:40 kg N:P₂O₅:K₂O per ha** together with **apply 10–12 t/ha fym/compost before puddling** and micronutrients **znso₄ 25 kg/ha at transplanting where zinc deficiency (khaira) is seen**. Apply nutrients in splits as per n in 3 splits: basal, active tillering, panicle initiation for efficient uptake; for legumes the fixed nitrogen reduces external nitrogen requirement.

details.title: Weed Management
details.content: **Echinochloa, Cyperus, Leptochloa sp. compete in the first 45 days. Control follows an integrated approach: **Integrated: puddling, stale seedbed, hand weeding at 20–25 DAP; pre-emergence pretilachlor 0.75 kg a.i./ha or bispyribac-sodium POST.**. Weed-free first 30–60 days (critical period) gives maximum yield advantage.

details.title: Pest Management
details.content: Major pests: **Yellow stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas), BPH (Nilaparvata lugens), leaf folder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis), whorl maggot, rice hispa.** Integrated Pest Management (IPM): monitor with traps/visual scouting, conserve natural enemies, and apply need-based pesticides at economic threshold levels.

details.title: Disease Management
details.content: Common diseases: **Blast (Pyricularia), sheath blight (Rhizoctonia), bacterial leaf blight (Xanthomonas), brown spot (Helminthosporium).** Prevention: disease-free seed/planting material, sanitation, resistant varieties, need-based fungicides/bio-control and balanced irrigation to keep foliage dry.

details.title: Plant Growth Management
details.content: Plant-growth management includes **keep water level shallow at tillering (3 cm), deeper at pi (5–10 cm); plant density and n-split guard against lodging.**. Remove off-types/diseased plants (roguing), avoid over-crowding, and provide support (staking/training) suited to the crop habit.

details.title: Crop Monitoring
details.content: Monitor periodically: **Weekly: plant stand, tiller count, leaf colour (N), standing water, pest/disease scouting at tillering, PI, flowering.** Record observations stage-wise and act early on pest/disease thresholds rather than after damage becomes visible.

details.title: Harvest & Post-harvest
details.content: Harvest at **grain turns golden, 22–25% moisture**. **Harvest by combine/mower at 22–25% MC; thresh, dry to 14% moisture**; expected yield about **5–8 t/ha (irrigated); 45–60 q/ha common for PR/IR hybrids**. Handle produce carefully to avoid bruising; dry to safe moisture and **Dry grain to ≤14% MC, store in gunny bags in clean, rat-free godown**.

details.title: Economics & Marketing
details.content: Typical input cost: **₹50,000–70,000/ha**. Prevailing market price **₹2,200–2,800/q (milled); MSP ₹2,300+/q**; expected net **Profit ₹25,000–45,000/ha**. **Sold through MSP / FCI procurement or local mandi**

details.title: Crop Basics & Plant Biology
details.content: **Maize (मक्का)** is a cereal crop belonging to the family **Poaceae** (scientific name *Zea mays*). It completes its crop cycle in about **95–120 days**. Growth stages follow the sequence germination → seedling → vegetative growth → reproductive phase (flowering/fruiting) → maturity. Main growing states: **Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra**. Popular varieties/ hybrids: **PMH-1, PMH-3, HQPM-1, DKC-9108, HM-4 (quality protein maize)**.

details.title: Climate Requirements
details.content: **Maize** thrives in a warm-season crop; 21–30 °C ideal, frost-sensitive climate with full sun; day-length neutral hybrids do well conditions. Ideal temperature range is **18–32 °C**, relative humidity **55–75%**, and annual rainfall **500–1200 mm**. Extreme conditions (frost, heat waves, hail or waterlogging) at sensitive stages lower yield and quality.

details.title: Soil Requirements
details.content: The crop grows best in **well-drained sandy-loam to loam with good fertility**. Suitable soil pH ranges from **5.5–7.5**, electrical conductivity (EC) below **<1.5 dS/m**, and organic matter of about **0.8–1.5%**. Adequate soil depth, good drainage, and balanced nutrient status of the soil are prerequisites for a healthy stand.

details.title: Land Preparation
details.content: Land preparation includes **plough + 2 harrowings, bed or ridge preparation; ridges (60 cm) improve drainage and mechanised picking.**. A well-tilled but properly levelled seedbed ensures uniform germination and stand establishment; drainage channels protect against waterlogging in heavy soil and during monsoons.

details.title: Seed & Planting Material
details.content: Use certified material: **Certified hybrid seed; treat with Thiram/Captan 2 g/kg against seed rot and downy mildew.**. Seed/variant rate for main season is **18–20 kg/ha (hybrids); 22–25 kg/ha composites**. Treat seed against soil-borne diseases and, where applicable, inoculate with beneficial rhizobia/PSB before sowing for legumes.

details.title: Sowing & Planting
details.content: **Sowing/planting season:** Kharif: Jun–Jul; Rabi: Oct–Nov (irrigated). Optimum sowing depth **5–6 cm**, spacing **60 × 20 cm one seed/hill**, maintaining a plant population of **≈ 65,000–75,000 plants/ha**. Correct spacing balances canopy (sunlight) and aeration. Depth and timing should follow regional package-of-practice recommendations.

details.title: Water & Irrigation Management
details.content: Irrigation method: **Furrow / drip / sprinkler; maize is water-efficient if timed**. Critical stages — Critical: knee-high, tasselling, silking and grain-fill; avoid stress at silking. Typical frequency/quantity: **6–9 irrigations depending on monsoon**. Do not let the crop suffer at the most sensitive growth phases (critical: knee-high, tasselling, silking and grain-fill; avoid stress at silking); avoid both drought and waterlogging.

details.title: Nutrient Management
details.content: Nutrient schedule: **150:75:60 kg N:P₂O₅:K₂O per ha (high-yield hybrids)** together with **8–10 t/ha fym 2 weeks before sowing** and micronutrients **znso₄ 20–25 kg/ha on zinc-deficient soils**. Apply nutrients in splits as per n in 3 splits; p & k basal in bands 5 cm below seed for efficient uptake; for legumes the fixed nitrogen reduces external nitrogen requirement.

details.title: Weed Management
details.content: **Cyperus rotundus, Echinochloa, Amaranthus, Sorghum halepense. Control follows an integrated approach: **Pre-emergence atrazine 1.0 kg a.i./ha at 0–3 DAS; inter-cultivation (hoeing) at 15 DAS + hand weeding 30 DAS.**. Weed-free first 30–60 days (critical period) gives maximum yield advantage.

details.title: Pest Management
details.content: Major pests: **Fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda), stem borer (Chilo partellus), shoot fly, cob worm (Helicoverpa).** Integrated Pest Management (IPM): monitor with traps/visual scouting, conserve natural enemies, and apply need-based pesticides at economic threshold levels.

details.title: Disease Management
details.content: Common diseases: **Turcicum leaf blight, stalk rot (Erwinia/Fusarium), downy mildew, rust, banded leaf & sheath blight.** Prevention: disease-free seed/planting material, sanitation, resistant varieties, need-based fungicides/bio-control and balanced irrigation to keep foliage dry.

details.title: Plant Growth Management
details.content: Plant-growth management includes **avoid n lodging with balanced k; ridge earthing-up at 30 das; remove off-types/de-tassel male rows in hybrid seed fields.**. Remove off-types/diseased plants (roguing), avoid over-crowding, and provide support (staking/training) suited to the crop habit.

details.title: Crop Monitoring
details.content: Monitor periodically: **Stand count at 7 DAS, weed pressure, leaf colour, whorl injury (FAW), silk emergence, moisture stress at silking.** Record observations stage-wise and act early on pest/disease thresholds rather than after damage becomes visible.

details.title: Harvest & Post-harvest
details.content: Harvest at **black layer at grain base, husk dry, grain 25–30% mc**. **Pick cobs, de-husk, dry to 14% MC, shell**; expected yield about **6–9 t/ha hybrids; QPM 6.5–8 t/ha**. Handle produce carefully to avoid bruising; dry to safe moisture and **Shelled grain at ≤14% MC in fumigated bags**.

details.title: Economics & Marketing
details.content: Typical input cost: **₹45,000–60,000/ha**. Prevailing market price **₹1,800–2,300/q**; expected net **Profit ₹20,000–35,000/ha**. **Poultry-feed millers, starch industries, ethanol plants buy most maize**

details.title: Crop Basics & Plant Biology
details.content: **Chickpea (चना (बंगाल चना))** is a pulse / legume belonging to the family **Fabaceae** (scientific name *Cicer arietinum*). It completes its crop cycle in about **110–140 days**. Growth stages follow the sequence germination → seedling → vegetative growth → reproductive phase (flowering/fruiting) → maturity. Main growing states: **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Haryana**. Popular varieties/ hybrids: **JG-315, JG-11, Pusa-372, Desi & Kabuli types, RVG-202**.

details.title: Climate Requirements
details.content: **Chickpea** thrives in a cool, dry rabi climate; 18–27 °C ideal; frost tolerant to light frost climate with full sun; short-day type conditions. Ideal temperature range is **15–30 °C**, relative humidity **40–60%**, and annual rainfall **400–900 mm**. Extreme conditions (frost, heat waves, hail or waterlogging) at sensitive stages lower yield and quality.

details.title: Soil Requirements
details.content: The crop grows best in **well-drained sandy-loam to medium black soil**. Suitable soil pH ranges from **6–7.5**, electrical conductivity (EC) below **<1.0 dS/m**, and organic matter of about **0.8–1.2%**. Adequate soil depth, good drainage, and balanced nutrient status of the soil are prerequisites for a healthy stand.

details.title: Land Preparation
details.content: Land preparation includes **well pulverised seedbed; 2 harrowings; avoid over-flooding; raised beds improve drainage in black soils.**. A well-tilled but properly levelled seedbed ensures uniform germination and stand establishment; drainage channels protect against waterlogging in heavy soil and during monsoons.

details.title: Seed & Planting Material
details.content: Use certified material: **Certified seed; inoculate with Rhizobium + PSB (250–350 g/ha) and treat with carbendazim.**. Seed/variant rate for main season is **60–75 kg/ha (desi), 80–90 kg (kabuli)**. Treat seed against soil-borne diseases and, where applicable, inoculate with beneficial rhizobia/PSB before sowing for legumes.

details.title: Sowing & Planting
details.content: **Sowing/planting season:** Rabi: mid-Oct to mid-Nov. Optimum sowing depth **8–10 cm**, spacing **30 × 10 cm (30 cm rows)**, maintaining a plant population of **≈ 3,00,000–4,00,000 plants/ha**. Correct spacing balances canopy (sunlight) and aeration. Depth and timing should follow regional package-of-practice recommendations.

details.title: Water & Irrigation Management
details.content: Irrigation method: **Sprinkler / surface; chickpea is largely rainfed/limited-irrigation**. Critical stages — One critical irrigation at pod-filling & flowering; avoid irrigation near maturity. Typical frequency/quantity: **1–2 protective irrigations**. Do not let the crop suffer at the most sensitive growth phases (one critical irrigation at pod-filling & flowering; avoid irrigation near maturity); avoid both drought and waterlogging.

details.title: Nutrient Management
details.content: Nutrient schedule: **20:50:20 kg N:P₂O₅:K₂O per ha (P is key)** together with **2.5–5 t/ha fym** and micronutrients **rhizobium inoculation provides n; apply 20 kg n as starter**. Apply nutrients in splits as per full p & k basal; no top-dress of n needed (self-sufficient via symbiosis) for efficient uptake; for legumes the fixed nitrogen reduces external nitrogen requirement.

details.title: Weed Management
details.content: **Chenopodium album, Asphodelus tenuifolius, Convolvulus arvensis. Control follows an integrated approach: **Pre-plant glyphosate for Asphodelus; hand weeding 25–30 DAS; pendimethalin 1.0 kg a.i./ha pre-emergence.**. Weed-free first 30–60 days (critical period) gives maximum yield advantage.

details.title: Pest Management
details.content: Major pests: **Gram pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera), cutworm, pod fly, aphids.** Integrated Pest Management (IPM): monitor with traps/visual scouting, conserve natural enemies, and apply need-based pesticides at economic threshold levels.

details.title: Disease Management
details.content: Common diseases: **Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris), Ascochyta blight, dry root rot, Botrytis grey mould.** Prevention: disease-free seed/planting material, sanitation, resistant varieties, need-based fungicides/bio-control and balanced irrigation to keep foliage dry.

details.title: Plant Growth Management
details.content: Plant-growth management includes **seed inoculation replaces n dose; avoid excessive vegetative growth by balanced sowing time; border/true-to-type roguing.**. Remove off-types/diseased plants (roguing), avoid over-crowding, and provide support (staking/training) suited to the crop habit.

details.title: Crop Monitoring
details.content: Monitor periodically: **Germination, nodulation check at 30 DAS, pod borer egg scouting (pheromone traps), wilt patches, crop-water relations.** Record observations stage-wise and act early on pest/disease thresholds rather than after damage becomes visible.

details.title: Harvest & Post-harvest
details.content: Harvest at **leaves dry, pods turn straw-yellow**. **Uproot/thresh; dry to 10% MC**; expected yield about **12–20 q/ha (desi 14–18 q, Kabuli 15–20 q)**. Handle produce carefully to avoid bruising; dry to safe moisture and **Clean dry grain, treat against bruchids with deltamethrin dust**.

details.title: Economics & Marketing
details.content: Typical input cost: **₹25,000–35,000/ha**. Prevailing market price **₹4,500–6,500/q**; expected net **Profit ₹30,000–50,000/ha**. **High MSP demand; export of kabuli to SE Asia/West Asia**

details.title: Crop Basics & Plant Biology
details.content: **Kidney Beans (राजमा)** is a pulse / legume belonging to the family **Fabaceae** (scientific name *Phaseolus vulgaris*). It completes its crop cycle in about **90–120 days**. Growth stages follow the sequence germination → seedling → vegetative growth → reproductive phase (flowering/fruiting) → maturity. Main growing states: **Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir, Maharashtra, Nagaland**. Popular varieties/ hybrids: **KRC-1, KR-143, Pusa Himlata, VRF-16, Uttara (for Uttarakhand)**.

details.title: Climate Requirements
details.content: **Kidney Beans** thrives in a cool, humid hill climate; 15–24 °C optimum; sensitive to heat & frost climate with full sun conditions. Ideal temperature range is **15–27 °C**, relative humidity **55–70%**, and annual rainfall **500–1000 mm**. Extreme conditions (frost, heat waves, hail or waterlogging) at sensitive stages lower yield and quality.

details.title: Soil Requirements
details.content: The crop grows best in **deep, fertile sandy-loam; good drainage vital**. Suitable soil pH ranges from **6–7**, electrical conductivity (EC) below **<1.0 dS/m**, and organic matter of about **1.0–1.5%**. Adequate soil depth, good drainage, and balanced nutrient status of the soil are prerequisites for a healthy stand.

details.title: Land Preparation
details.content: Land preparation includes **terraced hillsides prepared with 2 ploughings; ridge or bed system in heavy soils.**. A well-tilled but properly levelled seedbed ensures uniform germination and stand establishment; drainage channels protect against waterlogging in heavy soil and during monsoons.

details.title: Seed & Planting Material
details.content: Use certified material: **Certified seed; Rhizobium phaseoli inoculation + seed dressing for halo blight.**. Seed/variant rate for main season is **60–80 kg/ha**. Treat seed against soil-borne diseases and, where applicable, inoculate with beneficial rhizobia/PSB before sowing for legumes.

details.title: Sowing & Planting
details.content: **Sowing/planting season:** Kharif: May–Jul (hill regions); spring in lower hills. Optimum sowing depth **5–6 cm**, spacing **45 × 15 cm (2 seeds/hill)**, maintaining a plant population of **≈ 2,50,000 plant/ha**. Correct spacing balances canopy (sunlight) and aeration. Depth and timing should follow regional package-of-practice recommendations.

details.title: Water & Irrigation Management
details.content: Irrigation method: **Light surface irrigation; avoid over-irrigation (root rot)**. Critical stages — Critical at flowering & pod fill. Typical frequency/quantity: **2–4 irrigations**. Do not let the crop suffer at the most sensitive growth phases (critical at flowering & pod fill); avoid both drought and waterlogging.

details.title: Nutrient Management
details.content: Nutrient schedule: **20:60:30 kg N:P₂O₅:K₂O per ha** together with **fym 5–10 t/ha at land prep** and micronutrients **mo foliar spray 0.05% on acidic hilly soils**. Apply nutrients in splits as per p basal; n top-dressed once at pre-flowering if growth is poor for efficient uptake; for legumes the fixed nitrogen reduces external nitrogen requirement.

details.title: Weed Management
details.content: **Amaranthus, Echinochloa, Cyperus on terraces. Control follows an integrated approach: **Inter-culture + hand weeding 20–30 DAS; pendimethalin pre-emergence where available.**. Weed-free first 30–60 days (critical period) gives maximum yield advantage.

details.title: Pest Management
details.content: Major pests: **Aphids, whiteflies (vectors), pod borers, stem flies.** Integrated Pest Management (IPM): monitor with traps/visual scouting, conserve natural enemies, and apply need-based pesticides at economic threshold levels.

details.title: Disease Management
details.content: Common diseases: **Anthracnose (Colletotrichum lindemuthianum), common bacterial blight, rust, root rot (Rhizoctonia).** Prevention: disease-free seed/planting material, sanitation, resistant varieties, need-based fungicides/bio-control and balanced irrigation to keep foliage dry.

details.title: Plant Growth Management
details.content: Plant-growth management includes **staking needed in indeterminate types; balanced k for pod set; avoid dense canopy for disease escape.**. Remove off-types/diseased plants (roguing), avoid over-crowding, and provide support (staking/training) suited to the crop habit.

details.title: Crop Monitoring
details.content: Monitor periodically: **Germination %, nodulation, anthracnose spots on pods, irrigation at flowering, harvest-timing watch.** Record observations stage-wise and act early on pest/disease thresholds rather than after damage becomes visible.

details.title: Harvest & Post-harvest
details.content: Harvest at **pods dry, beans rattle**. **Uproot, dry, thresh; sun dry to 10% MC**; expected yield about **16–24 q/ha (hill conditions)**. Handle produce carefully to avoid bruising; dry to safe moisture and **Store at ≤10% MC with proper fumigation against bruchids**.

details.title: Economics & Marketing
details.content: Typical input cost: **₹30,000–40,000/ha**. Prevailing market price **₹65,000–1,10,000/q (or ₹65–110/kg)**; expected net **High-value crop with strong demand in North India**. **Sold as dry beans; winter demand from Kashmir/north Indian plains**

details.title: Crop Basics & Plant Biology
details.content: **Pigeonpea (अरहर (तूर))** is a pulse / legume belonging to the family **Fabaceae** (scientific name *Cajanus cajan*). It completes its crop cycle in about **150–210 days**. details.title: Climate Requirements
details.content: **Pigeonpea** thrives in a warm kharif crop; 24–32 °C ideal; drought-tolerant once established (deep tap root) climate with full sun conditions. details.title: Soil Requirements

details.title: Land Preparation

details.title: Seed & Planting Material
details.content: Use certified material: **Certified seed + Rhizobium cowpea-group inoculation; carbendazim seed dressing.**. Seed/variant rate for main season is **12–15 kg/ha**. Treat seed against soil-borne diseases and, where applicable, inoculate with beneficial rhizobia/PSB before sowing for legumes.

details.title: Sowing & Planting
details.content: **Sowing/planting season:** Kharif: Jun–Jul (first fortnight of June in central India). Depth and timing should follow regional package-of-practice recommendations.

details.title: Water & Irrigation Management
details.content: Irrigation method: **Mostly rainfed; protective irrigation only**. Critical stages — Critical: flowering and pod initiation. Typical frequency/quantity: **1–2 supplementary irrigations in dry years**. Do not let the crop suffer at the most sensitive growth phases (critical: flowering and pod initiation); avoid both drought and waterlogging.

details.title: Nutrient Management
details.content: Nutrient schedule: **25:60:40 kg N:P₂O₅:K₂O per ha** together with **fym 5 t/ha** and micronutrients **seed inoculation covers n; s & b on deficient soils**. Apply nutrients in splits as per full p/k basal; n only as starter for efficient uptake; for legumes the fixed nitrogen reduces external nitrogen requirement.

details.title: Weed Management
details.content: **Commelina, Echinochloa, Celosia, Cyperus in early growth. Control follows an integrated approach: **Inter-cultivation 20 & 40 DAS + hand weeding; pendimethalin 1.0 kg pre-emergence.**. Weed-free first 30–60 days (critical period) gives maximum yield advantage.

details.title: Pest Management
details.content: Major pests: **Pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera), pod fly (Melanagromyza), plume moth, blue butterfly.** Integrated Pest Management (IPM): monitor with traps/visual scouting, conserve natural enemies, and apply need-based pesticides at economic threshold levels.

details.title: Disease Management

details.title: Plant Growth Management

details.title: Crop Monitoring
details.content: Monitor periodically: **Wilt screening, sterility-mosaic roguing, pheromone traps for pod borer, moisture check at flowering.** Record observations stage-wise and act early on pest/disease thresholds rather than after damage becomes visible.

details.title: Harvest & Post-harvest
details.content: Harvest at **80–90% pods turn brown**. **Cut plants, dry 7–10 days, thresh**; expected yield about **12–18 q/ha**. Handle produce carefully to avoid bruising; dry to safe moisture and **Store dal/pods at ≤10% MC in sealed bins**.

details.title: Economics & Marketing

details.title: Crop Basics & Plant Biology
details.content: **Moth Beans (मोठ)** is a pulse / legume (dryland) belonging to the family **Fabaceae** (scientific name *Vigna aconitifolia*). It completes its crop cycle in about **75–90 days**. Growth stages follow the sequence germination → seedling → vegetative growth → reproductive phase (flowering/fruiting) → maturity. Main growing states: **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh**. Popular varieties/ hybrids: **RMO-40, RMO-71, Jwala, Krishna, Rameshwar (for arid belt)**.

details.title: Climate Requirements
details.content: **Moth Beans** thrives in a hot-arid crop; 26–40 °C; thrives on low & erratic rainfall; very drought tolerant climate with full sun conditions. Ideal temperature range is **24–40 °C**, relative humidity **40–55%**, and annual rainfall **300–600 mm**. Extreme conditions (frost, heat waves, hail or waterlogging) at sensitive stages lower yield and quality.

details.title: Soil Requirements
details.content: The crop grows best in **light sandy / loamy-sand soils of arid rajasthan**. Suitable soil pH ranges from **6–8**, electrical conductivity (EC) below **up to 2.5 dS/m (salt tolerant)**, and organic matter of about **0.3–0.6%**. Adequate soil depth, good drainage, and balanced nutrient status of the soil are prerequisites for a healthy stand.

details.title: Land Preparation
details.content: Land preparation includes **minimal tillage — one harrowing; conserve moisture with light mulching; rainfed on stored soil moisture.**. Adequate soil depth, good drainage, and balanced nutrient status of the soil are prerequisites for a healthy stand.

details.title: Land Preparation
details.content: Land preparation includes **terrace on slopes (1–2% grade outward); contour planting 2.5×2.5 m; shade-tree belt before planting crop.**. A well-tilled but properly levelled seedbed ensures uniform germination and stand establishment; drainage channels protect against waterlogging in heavy soil and during monsoons.

details.title: Seed & Planting Material
details.content: Use certified material: **Certified bean seed/cuttings; arabica from fresh parchment; robusta from healthy clones.**. Seed/variant rate for main season is **n/a — 1,600–2,000 plants/ha (monocrop), 1,200 under shade**. Treat seed against soil-borne diseases and, where applicable, inoculate with beneficial rhizobia/PSB before sowing for legumes.

details.title: Sowing & Planting
details.content: **Sowing/planting season:** undefined. Optimum sowing depth **Set at one node above soil in pits**, spacing **2.5 × 2.5 m under 9 × 9 m shade grid**, maintaining a plant population of **1,200–2,000 plants/ha**. Correct spacing balances canopy (sunlight) and aeration. Depth and timing should follow regional package-of-practice recommendations.

details.title: Water & Irrigation Management
details.content: Irrigation method: **Rainfed under shade; drip later addition on plant setback**. Critical stages — Critical: blossom showers (Mar–Apr) & berry setting (Apr–May). Typical frequency/quantity: **0–2 light nfluence irrigations**. Do not let the crop suffer at the most sensitive growth phases (critical: blossom showers (mar–apr) & berry setting (apr–may)); avoid both drought and waterlogging.

details.title: Nutrient Management
details.content: Nutrient schedule: **150:60:60 kg N:P₂O₅:K₂O per ha incl. organic cake supplements** together with **10 kg fym/plant + coffee husk compost + green manures** and micronutrients **zn, b on high altitude; lime/amendment for very acid**. Apply nutrients in splits as per 3 splits jan, may, sep for efficient uptake; for legumes the fixed nitrogen reduces external nitrogen requirement.

details.title: Weed Management
details.content: **Annual + perennial weeds harbour bugs. Control follows an integrated approach: **3 mechanical weedings Apr–Oct + mulching; glyphosate for perennial weeds (sheltered).**. Weed-free first 30–60 days (critical period) gives maximum yield advantage.

details.title: Pest Management
details.content: Major pests: **Coffee berry borer (Hypothenemus), white stem borer (arabica), mealy bugs, shot hole borer, mites.** Integrated Pest Management (IPM): monitor with traps/visual scouting, conserve natural enemies, and apply need-based pesticides at economic threshold levels.

details.title: Disease Management
details.content: Common diseases: **Coffee leaf rust (Hemileia, arabica), black rot, root diseases, berry blight; robusta resistant to rust.** Prevention: disease-free seed/planting material, sanitation, resistant varieties, need-based fungicides/bio-control and balanced irrigation to keep foliage dry.

details.title: Plant Growth Management
details.content: Plant-growth management includes **shade management (silver oak pollarding); pruning crooked bearers; borer control & timely harvest; two-peak monosson.**. Remove off-types/diseased plants (roguing), avoid over-crowding, and provide support (staking/training) suited to the crop habit.

details.title: Crop Monitoring
details.content: Monitor periodically: **Borer beetle galleries on cherries, rust leaf spots on lower canopy, mist-damps at flowering, berry drop counting.** Record observations stage-wise and act early on pest/disease thresholds rather than after damage becomes visible.

details.title: Harvest & Post-harvest
details.content: Harvest at **cherries turn red (5–7 months arabica); selective picking at intervals**. **Hand pick red cherries; wet method for parchment; sun/polisher drying**; expected yield about **Arabica 800–1,200 kg/ha green; robusta 1,200–2,000 kg/ha**. Handle produce carefully to avoid bruising; dry to safe moisture and **Green beans grade & export; store at 10–12% MC, cool dry godown**.

details.title: Economics & Marketing
details.content: Typical input cost: **Establishment ₹4–6 lakh/ha (incl. shade)**. Prevailing market price **₹250–400/kg green (arabica premium)**; expected net **₹2–4 lakh/ha mature**. **Coffee Board auction; exports to EU/West; artisanal roasters growing**
